main_text.p: Est igitur Evangelium solenne Christi Gratiæ à seculo abscondita, præconium seu revelatio, facta primum voce ipsius Christi & apostolorum, & miraculis confirmata: deinde verò vt continuo progressu eius veritas seculis omnibus superstes esset in mundo, ab Evangelistis & Apostolis diuinitus inspiratis, mandata literis, & publicis quasi tabulis consignata, ad perfectam Ecclesiæ in doctrina salutis institutionem.

Proprium igitur Euangelicæ historiæ subiectum est, Christus θεάνθρωπος, diuinæ in nos misericordiæ ac fauoris pignus; cuius incarnationem, doctrinam & gesta, mortem & resurrectionem, & in cœlos ascensum, & horum omnium fructum & finem, hoc est personam & officium, meritum & efficaciam Christi, θεόπνευστοι Amanuenses, hoc est quatuor illi Evangelistæ, magno consensu exponunt.

Evangelistas igitur hoc loco vocamus, non in genere omnes eos qui tradiderunt doctrinam de Messia, in qua significatione vox illa accipitur Eph. 4. & 2. Sed in specie authenticos scriptores historiæ de persona & officio Christi in carnati: Historici certissimi, verissimi. Vide Luc. 1. v. 2. & 4. & Ioh. 21. v. 24. licet inter eos emineat propter argumenti sublimitatem de Christi diuinitate Iohannes.

Scopus seu finis huius historiæ proximus est, demonstrare, Quod hic Iesus Nazarenus Mariæ filius, sit Christus ille Dei filius, ac Saluator Mundi. Scopus principalis, cui proximus ille subordinatus est atque inseruit, est: Adducere clugg

page.notes: The marginal words "Adducere" and the following word are in a small, heavily inked hand in the right margin; they are printed in italic-like type and are kept as a note. The last word at the right margin ("clugg") is doubtful: the letters are blurred and could be a catchword-like fragment or a printer's note; not certain. The final line of the page, "subordinatus est atque inseruit, est:", is in a heavier, blurred type, possibly a smudge or print damage; readings of "inseruit" and "est" are uncertain. "Iohannes" and "Nazarenus" read as printed. The Greek words θεάνθρωπος and θεόπνευστοι are written as best read from the scan and may be imperfect. The facing page is cut off at the right edge and is not transcribed.
